title: Global military spending rise continues as European and Asian expenditures surge
date_evidence: (Stockholm, 27 April 2026) World military expenditure reached $2887 billion in 2025, an increase of 2.9 per cent in real terms over 2024.
key_claim: World military spending hit $2887bn in 2025; Europe rose 14% to $864bn, the sharpest annual growth in Central and Western Europe since the cold war, while US spending fell 7.5%.
signals_supported: NATO 5% spending target and European rearmament
US conventional commitment to European defence
verbatim_quote: military spending by European NATO members rose faster than at any time since 1953

title: The Hague Summit Declaration
date_evidence: The Hague Summit Declaration | NATO Official text, official-texts/2025/06/25/the-hague-summit-declaration: Allies commit to invest 5% of GDP annually on core defence and security-related spending by 2035.
key_claim: NATO Allies committed at The Hague to invest 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core defence plus up to 1.5% security and resilience), with a 2029 review.
signals_supported: NATO 5% spending target and European rearmament

title: Commission increases submarine cable security with a EUR 347 million investment and new Cable Security Toolbox
date_evidence: On February 5, 2026, the European Commission introduced a new Cable Security Toolbox of risk mitigating measures and a list of Cable Projects of European Interest, allocating EUR 347 million to strategic submarine cable projects.
key_claim: The EU launched a EUR 347 million Cable Security Toolbox and 13 Cable Projects of European Interest, the largest EU investment to date in subsea cable protection.

title: Allied Air Command leads counter-drone training over the Baltics under Eastern Sentry
date_evidence: NATO Allied Air Command (AIRCOM) led counter-drone training over Lithuania and Latvia on May 27, 2026, as part of enhanced Vigilance Activity (eVA) Eastern Sentry.
key_claim: Under Eastern Sentry, NATO ran layered counter-UAS training over the Baltics integrating F-16s, Lithuanian SBAMD, Spanish NASAMS and a Romanian Patriot; an April Crucible event tested 250-plus counter-drone systems.

title: Seabed zero: Baltic sabotage and the global risks to undersea infrastructure
key_claim: Western economies depend on data and energy along the seafloor; Russia and China are weaponising that dependency, and legal gaps under UNCLOS frustrate prosecution of foreign-flagged vessels.

title: Global defence spending continues to grow amid geopolitical uncertainty (Military Balance 2026)
date_evidence: iiss.org/online-analysis/military-balance/2026/02/global-defence-spending-continues-to-grow-amid-geopolitical-uncertainty: European spending rose to almost USD563 billion in 2025, a 12.6% year-on-year increase (Military Balance 2026, February 2026).
key_claim: European defence spending reached almost USD563bn in 2025 (+12.6%), but the IISS estimates replacing US conventional capabilities in the Euro-Atlantic theatre could cost around USD1 trillion, and several allies will struggle to meet NATO targets.
signals_supported: NATO 5% spending target and European rearmament

title: Europe's Defense Factories: More Urgency Please
key_claim: EDIP has the right architecture but deliveries are expected from 2028 and lines uncertified before 2033; SAFE demand (19 of 27 states) exceeded budget, and Russia produced four million shells last year versus Europe's two million.
signals_supported: European industrial capacity to meet demand

title: European Commission adopts $1.7B work program to ramp up weapons production
date_evidence: By Tim Martin on March 30, 2026 2:56 pm
key_claim: The EC adopted a EUR 1.5bn EDIP work programme: over EUR 700m to ramp counter-drone, missile and ammunition production, EUR 260m for Ukraine, plus joint procurement and a EUR 100m defence start-up equity facility.

title: Defense tech startups had their best funding year ever in 2025
key_claim: Venture capital deals in defence technology jumped to a record $49.1bn in 2025 from $27.2bn a year earlier (PitchBook); equity funding more than doubled to $17.9bn (CB Insights), with autonomy and AI the focus.

title: Explained: How drone incursions in Europe went from rarity to reality
key_claim: A Romanian drone strike reignited fears that Russia's war is spilling into Europe as incursions multiply across NATO and EU states, blending military pressure, disruption and psychological warfare.

title: US tells Europe, Canada to boost NATO air and naval forces
key_claim: After Washington cut its contribution to the NATO Force Model, the number of US fighter jets available to NATO is set to fall by a third, with fewer destroyers and no submarines, and Europe must provide its own reconnaissance drones.
signals_supported: US conventional commitment to European defence

title: Russia stepping up hybrid attacks, preparing for long standoff with West, Dutch intelligence warns
date_evidence: Alexander Martin February 20th, 2026 - Russia stepping up hybrid attacks, preparing for long standoff with West, Dutch intelligence warns
key_claim: Dutch AIVD and MIVD warn Russia is intensifying a hybrid campaign of cyberattacks, sabotage and disinformation, with rising risk tolerance since 2024; they also note many Baltic cable breaks were likely accidental.
signals_supported: Hybrid threats, sabotage and resilience rules

title: Defence startups draw EUR 8bn to Europe's hottest tech investment spot
key_claim: European defence, security and resilience startups raised a record EUR 8bn in 2025, up 55% year on year; ISR and space soaked up 44% of capital and late-stage rounds tripled to EUR 4.3bn (Dealroom/NATO Innovation Fund).
